q: A hospital's patient records are secretly modified by an unauthorised person. Which principle of the CIA triad is violated?
exp: Unauthorised modification of data violates integrity, which ensures data stays accurate and unaltered.

q: Using a Caesar cipher with key 3, the plaintext CAT is encrypted as
exp: Each letter shifts 3 places forward: C→F, A→D, T→W.

q: Which malware spreads across a network by copying itself, without needing a host file or any user action?
exp: A worm is self-replicating and standalone; a virus needs a host file and a trojan does not replicate.

q: Under the IT Act 2000 (as amended in 2008), which section deals with punishment for identity theft?
exp: Section 66C punishes fraudulent or dishonest use of another person's password, digital signature or unique identification feature.

q: A packet-filtering firewall makes its decisions mainly by examining
options: The full text of e-mail bodies
The physical condition of network cables
IP addresses and port numbers in packet headers
exp: Packet filters inspect header fields such as source/destination IP address, port and protocol against rules.

q: Which statement correctly describes AES?
exp: AES (Rijndael) works on 128-bit blocks and supports key lengths of 128, 192 and 256 bits.

q: An e-mail that appears to come from a bank asks the user to click a link and enter net-banking credentials on a look-alike page. This attack is called
exp: Tricking users via deceptive messages into revealing credentials on fake sites is phishing.

q: A differential backup copies
options: Only files changed since the most recent backup of any type
All files changed since the last full backup
Only the files deleted since the last full backup
exp: Differential backups grow each day because they always compare against the last full backup.

q: Which of the following is NOT a property of a cryptographic hash function?
options: It must be possible to recover the original message from its hash
It produces a fixed-length output for any input size
It is hard to find two inputs with the same hash
A tiny change in input changes the output drastically
exp: Hash functions are one-way; reversibility would defeat their purpose.

q: The "zero trust" security model is based on the principle
options: trust everything inside the corporate network
trust any user with a valid IP address
never trust, always verify every access request
trust devices that were once authenticated forever
exp: Zero trust authenticates and authorises each request regardless of network location.

q: In an RSA system p = 3, q = 11 and e = 7. The ciphertext for plaintext m = 2 is
An attacker sends a flood of TCP SYN packets and never completes the handshake, leaving the server with many half-open connections. This is a
exp: A SYN flood exhausts the server's connection table with half-open connections, denying service to legitimate users.

q: Which intrusion detection approach compares observed traffic with a database of known attack patterns?
exp: Signature-based IDS matches events against stored patterns of known attacks; anomaly-based IDS looks for deviations from a baseline.

q: Withdrawing money from an ATM using a debit card and a PIN is an example of
options: Two factors, both of the 'something you know' type
Two-factor authentication (something you have plus something you know)
exp: The card is something you have and the PIN is something you know, so two different factor categories are used.

q: An ethical (white-hat) hacker differs from a malicious hacker mainly because the ethical hacker
options: Sells stolen data to the highest bidder
Attacks systems to promote a political cause
Tests systems with the owner's authorisation to find and report weaknesses
Writes malware to infect public computers
exp: Authorisation and intent to improve security define ethical hacking.

q: A login query is: SELECT * FROM users WHERE name='$u' AND pass='$p'. An attacker enters admin' -- as the username and anything as the password. What is the likely result?
options: The password check is commented out and the attacker logs in as admin
The server always returns a syntax error
The password is automatically hashed and compared
exp: The quote closes the name string and -- starts a comment, so the AND pass condition is ignored.

q: Every pair among 20 users must share a distinct secret key for symmetric encryption. How many keys are needed?
Using several layers of controls (physical, network, host, application, data) so that failure of one layer does not expose the system is called
exp: Defence in depth layers independent controls so an attacker must defeat all of them.

q: The default TCP port used by HTTPS is
exp: HTTP uses 80, SSH 22 and SMTP 25; HTTPS (HTTP over TLS) uses 443.

q: A full backup is taken every Sunday and an incremental backup every night from Monday to Saturday. The system fails on Thursday morning. How many backup sets are needed to restore it?
exp: Restore requires the Sunday full plus incrementals of Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday: 1 + 3 = 4.

q: Match the IT Act sections: (i) 66E (ii) 66F (iii) 67B (iv) 66D with (p) cyber terrorism (q) cheating by personation using a computer resource (r) child sexually explicit material (s) violation of privacy.
exp: 66E is privacy violation, 66F cyber terrorism, 67B child pornography and 66D cheating by personation.

q: A digital signature is created by encrypting the message digest with the
exp: Only the sender holds the private key, so anyone can verify the signature with the sender's public key.

q: Files on a company server are renamed with a strange extension and a note demands payment in cryptocurrency for the decryption key. This malware is
exp: Ransomware encrypts victim data and demands a ransom.

q: Which of the following is NOT plagiarism?
options: Submitting an essay written by someone else as one's own
Copying paragraphs from a website without acknowledgement
Quoting a passage in quotation marks with a proper citation of the source
Presenting another researcher's idea in your own words without crediting them
exp: Properly quoted and cited material acknowledges the source; the others pass off others' work as one's own.

q: The primary purpose of a Virtual Private Network (VPN) is to
options: Increase the physical bandwidth of the link
Assign IP addresses dynamically to hosts
Create an encrypted tunnel for private communication over a public network
exp: A VPN uses tunnelling and encryption so that data crossing the Internet stays confidential.

q: An intrusion detection system that raises an alert after suspicious activity is an example of which type of security control?
exp: Detective controls (IDS, log monitoring, CCTV) discover incidents; preventive ones (firewall) stop them.

q: Which attack injects malicious client-side script into a web page that is later viewed by other users?
exp: XSS makes the victim's browser execute attacker-supplied script from a trusted site.

q: An X.509 digital certificate essentially binds
options: A private key to a user's password
The identity of an entity to its public key, signed by a Certificate Authority
A user name to a MAC address
An IP address to a domain's TTL value
exp: The CA signs the certificate to vouch that the public key belongs to the named subject.

q:
Statement I: In symmetric-key cryptography the same key is used for encryption and decryption.
Statement II: Asymmetric cryptography is generally faster than symmetric cryptography for bulk data.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
exp: Statement I is true. Public-key algorithms are far slower, so symmetric ciphers encrypt bulk data; Statement II is false.

q: In disaster recovery, the Recovery Time Objective (RTO) is
options: The maximum acceptable amount of data loss measured in time
The interval between two consecutive backups
The maximum acceptable time within which a service must be restored after a failure
The total cost of the backup system
exp: RTO is about downtime; the data-loss tolerance is the Recovery Point Objective.

q: In a man-in-the-middle attack, the attacker
options: Secretly sits between two communicating parties and can read or alter their messages
Floods the server with traffic to make it unavailable
Encrypts the victim's files and demands money
Guesses passwords using a word list
exp: MITM relays and possibly modifies communication while both ends believe they talk directly to each other.

q: Section 66A of the IT Act was struck down as unconstitutional by the Supreme Court in
options: Justice K. S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (2017)
Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978)
Shreya Singhal v. Union of India (2015)
exp: In Shreya Singhal (2015) the Court held Section 66A violated freedom of speech under Article 19(1)(a).

q: Which of the following is NOT a function of a firewall?
options: Repairing corrupted files on the hard disk
exp: A firewall controls and logs network traffic; it does not repair files.

q: In a TLS session, after the handshake the bulk application data is encrypted using
exp: Asymmetric methods establish the keys; fast symmetric encryption then protects the data.

q: In an RSA system n = 55 (p = 5, q = 11) and e = 3. The private exponent d is
Fraud carried out through voice calls in which a caller pretends to be a bank official to obtain OTPs is called
exp: Vishing is voice phishing; smishing uses SMS.

q: The output size of the SHA-256 hash function is
exp: SHA-256 yields a 256-bit digest (MD5 is 128 and SHA-1 is 160 bits).

q: The trail of data that a person leaves through online activities such as browsing, posting and purchasing is called the
exp: A digital footprint is the data trail created by one's online activity.

q: In a fraud, a program deducts very small amounts such as fractions of a rupee from thousands of accounts and credits them to the attacker. This is a
exp: Salami attacks slice off tiny amounts that individually go unnoticed.

q: The '3-2-1' backup rule recommends
options: 3 copies of data, on 2 different media, with 1 copy kept off-site
3 full backups, 2 incremental backups and 1 differential backup
3 backups per day, 2 per week and 1 per month
exp: Keeping three copies on two media types with one off-site guards against most failures.
